newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI sets banks' year-end valuation norms.
newsitem.headline: India RBI sets banks' year-end valuation norms.

text.p: The Reserve bank of India (RBI) said on Thursday it set a yield to maturity of 13.56 percent for ten-year securities for the purpose of year-end valuation of bank investments.
The RBI norms are used by banks to value their investments at market prices.
The RBI said in a statement that valuation of government securities should be done as per market quotations on March 31.
Where market quotations were not available, valuation of government securities should be made as per the prices on the RBI's price-list on March 31, the central bank said. RBI price-list on March 31
The RBI said the following yields might be applied for other government securities as on March 31:
No. of years Yield to maturity (%)
"We have to advise that if there is any appreciation in the value of securities on account of the method of valuation...it should not be booked as income," the RBI statement said.
The above yields should also be applied to state government and government securities, it said.
